title: Royal letters patent for Law's bank
established: Manuscript letters patent authorized Banque Générale. The museum identifies signing by Louis XV and Regent Philippe d'Orléans. Full French clauses require manuscript examination.
limitations: The charter's existence and institutional purpose are supported; loan disbursements, personal investors and full wording are not verified.

title: Order restricting paper-for-large-silver-coin exchange
established: The Council of State order restricted exchange of banknotes for large silver coins during Law's crisis.
limitations: An order is not a record of how many coins were actually exchanged, nor proof of any particular counterparty.

title: Royal order to inventory and burn designated banknotes
established: The edict names Baussan and Bertin as officials tasked with reporting on specified notes and ensuring their destruction.
limitations: No banknote destruction totals or completed burning certificates extracted from the original manuscript.

title: Hutcheson public letter challenging South Sea stock calculations
reference: Wellcome work yy3prd74; ECCO edition
established: A pamphlet by Archibald Hutcheson responds to share valuation printed in the White-Hall Evening-Post.
limitations: The bibliographic record identifies a public discussion, but no original numerical calculation or private recipient communication has been transcribed.

title: Satire showing John Law and Amsterdam's English coffee house
reference: Wellcome 811589i
established: An etching depicts share traders in an English coffee house in Amsterdam and includes a bust of John Law and the Parisian Quincampoix street reference.
limitations: Images satirize market life; depicted individuals or transactions must not be treated as verified actual trades.

title: Surviving Dutch Leydse Courant market coverage, 1719–1720
reference: Yale ICF 1720 Project, Leydse Courant image archive
established: Digitized issues cover 20 November 1719 through 30 December 1720, offering a dated source to test when news was printed in Dutch markets.
limitations: This atlas has not extracted any issue's specific quoted prices or communications; no information-lag estimate is claimed.

title: Stad Rotterdam transaction book begins recording financial activity
reference: Yale ICF, Stad Rotterdam Transaction Book, pp.1–300, July 16–24 1720
established: Yale indexes original Rotterdam discount-company transactions starting July 16, 1720 and books extending to 1723, which offer a route for reconstructing counterparties.
limitations: No named counterparty, transaction value or British/French security purchase is asserted without reading the ledger page.

title: Passenger list for Louisiana, January 1720–January 1721
reference: ANOM COL G1 464, 68 images, record 31224
established: Archive listing identifies a list of people registered for Louisiana voyages from Lorient over January 1720–January 1721.
limitations: The listing itself does not prove that each individual embarked, survived, was free or enslaved, arrived, or settled. Do not derive demographic totals.

place: Biloxi (Fort Louis de la Mobile vicinity)
title: Diron census of Mobile and surrounding settlements
reference: ANOM COL G1 464, 7 images, record 31234
established: Archive catalogue identifies a census organized by households, people categorized as servants/enslaved, and livestock.
limitations: The colonial categories dehumanized enslaved people and do not convey their names or experiences equally. Totals remain unverified.

title: Census of New Orleans and nearby concessions, appended to Diron's letter
reference: ANOM COL G1 464, 12 images, record 31235; attached letter dated 1722-01-02
established: A signed census reports people, French servants, enslaved laborers, and agricultural conditions; metadata identifies Diron and co-signers.
limitations: Neither demographic totals nor individual identity matches have been extracted, and colonial counts may exclude independent Indigenous communities.

title: English-language printed account explicitly describing Mr Law's Mississippi Company
reference: BnF Gallica ark:/12148/bpt6k109867v (scan fetch denied)
established: The BnF curated list identifies a 1720 English-language account of the French Mississippi Company, direct evidence that an English-language explanation circulated in print.
limitations: Publication place, author, readership, full argument, and involvement of South Sea directors remain unverified in this research pass.

title: Signed one-page manuscript acknowledging 20 bank-equity shares
reference: HNOC MSS 606 Folder 4, accession 2010.0158.20, PDF finding aid printed p. 2
established: Frenier signed a document certifying an unidentified bearer received twenty shares from Mr. Imbert, the Duke of Orléans's first valet. This is a verified archive description of a distinct 1719 financial instrument.
limitations: Full French note, price paid, previous holder's ownership and identity of the bearer were not independently read or established. Not evidence of an illicit coordinated network.

title: Original 50-livre Banque Générale bearer banknote
reference: HNOC MSS 606 Folder 3, accession 2010.0158.19, PDF finding aid printed p. 2
established: The archive lists an original banknote for fifty livres tournois, serial number handwritten, signed in print at Paris on September 2, 1720 by five named officials and promising payment to bearer.
limitations: Face value and promised redemption are not a record that any bearer redeemed the note. Names of actual holders, cash exchanged and later valuation have not been checked.

title: Second, expanded 1721 New Orleans census copy — ANOM 31236
reference: ANOM COL G1 464, 17-page catalogued document / 29 digital images; CABAC_PIAF_6928; item 31236
established: Archival catalogue explicitly labels this as apparently a copy of the previous 1721 New Orleans census, followed by more extensive information on land concessions and colony status.
limitations: No handwritten original folio, totals or population categories checked; this is a likely duplicate or extended companion and must not be counted as a second independent 1721 census.

title: Le Gac memoir: five parts including Indigenous and French village names
reference: ANOM FR CAOM 4DFC8, item 40699, 101-page memoir / 99 digital images
established: The colonial Company official Le Gac's memoir describes Louisiana at his arrival in 1718, his activities to 1721 and lists French and Indigenous villages on the Mississippi and tributaries.
limitations: The memoir's actual village names and descriptions are not independently extracted from the French manuscript. The official's reporting is not equivalent to Indigenous self-description or community-approved knowledge.

title: French letters describing Sainte-Catherine concession conflict with Natchez
reference: ANOM COL G1 465, item 31377, four digitized images, letters March 9–10 1722
established: Archival catalogue describes letters from French officers concerning an attack on the Sainte-Catherine concession by Natchez people and French armed-response discussions.
limitations: Only French administrative and settler perspectives in the catalogue have been inspected; no Natchez perspective, exact casualty numbers, or guilt conclusions can be established from this title.

title: Superior Council sends Choctaw trade concerns to Company of Indies
reference: Historic New Orleans Collection manuscript guide; AC C13, vol.9 p.51, 47-page copy, dated 1725-02-27; see separate C13A vol.9 fol.65v in Musco et al. (2025)
established: An archival guide describes a letter from the Louisiana Superior Council covering Choctaw trade alongside other colonial issues. Specific text and folios have not been inspected; relation to scholarship's French translation should be checked.
limitations: The 47-page original is not transcribed or quoted here. No original 1725 Choctaw petitions have been directly accessed and no Company decision or treasury disbursement is implied.

title: Diron d'Artaguiette correspondence on Périer and the Choctaw mission
reference: HNOC manuscript guide, AC C13 vol.12 p.362, nine-page original dated February 9–10 1730
established: The archive guide describes Diron's letter to the Controller General discussing Régis du Roullet's Choctaw visit, related conflict with Périer, and regional conditions. The date range is preserved.
limitations: The full original French nine pages have not been read, and the abstract does not verify financial award, local trade prices or actual compensation.

title: Ministry approves decision in Diron–Company dispute
reference: HNOC manuscript guide, AC B57 p.815, minister to Salmon, 2 September 1732, two-page original
established: A royal ministry letter approved a Superior Council decision regarding Diron and the Company of the Indies, according to the original correspondence inventory. It is a direct archival lead to legal confirmation.
limitations: The archive summary provides no monetary amount, payee receipt, payment instrument or identification of exact court judgment. Match to the 29,000-livre folios requires original examination.

title: Council folios cited for 29,000-livre monopoly compensation award
reference: ANOM C13A, 1732, folios 33–33v as cited by Musco, Ellis & Spring (2025) — original image not independently opened
established: A peer-reviewed study explicitly refers to the archival folios and describes a 29,000 French-livre compensation judgment for Bernard Diron d'Artaguiette after a challenged trade monopoly.
limitations: Only modern scholarly description of the archival folios inspected. The archival hand itself, judgment language, date and actual payment are all unverified.
